newsitem.title: USA: Lear says sees Q2 EPS cut by auto strikes.
newsitem.headline: Lear says sees Q2 EPS cut by auto strikes.

text.p: Lear Corp said its second quarter 1997 earnings per share will be hurt a continuing work stoppage at General Motors Corp's Pontiac East assembly plant and a recently concluded work stoppage at Chrysler Corp Mound Road engine plant.
"To date, earnings per share for the quarter ending June 28, 1997, have been adversely affected by approximately $0.09 per share due to these work stoppages," Lear said.
"Based upon these customers' current production schedules for the remainder of calendar 1997, the company believes there is limited potential for recovery of this amount," Lear said.
Lear is projected to earn about $0.97 per share in its second quarter, compared with $0.83 per share in the year-ago quarter, according to First Call's consensus of 12 brokers' forecasts.
Lear makes automotive supplies and had 1996 sales of more than $6.2 billion.
